paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: what's inside you shows up on the outside. Jesus says each tree is known by its own fruit, and that "out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks." (Luke 6:44-45) So the real question isn't how good we look on a tray. It's what's in the dough.

That's why the speck and the beam matter. Jesus calls the man who offers to fix his brother's eye while his own is blocked a hypocrite, and He says to take the beam out of your own eye first. (Luke 6:41-42) I'll be honest, I'm the first one to spot a crumb on YOUR apron while I'm wearing the whole bag. Jesus isn't telling us to stop caring about others. He's telling us to get clear ourselves, so we can see and help.

Then comes the question that gets me every time: "Why do you call Me 'Lord, Lord,' but do not do what I say?" (Luke 6:46) Hearing is not enough. The one who hears His words and acts on them is like the builder who dug deep and laid the foundation on the rock, and when the torrent came, the house stood. (Luke 6:47-49) So, baker, let's keep listening, keep doing, and keep building on Jesus, because that's a foundation no flood can shake.
